rules: Start the original pipeline wall clock before creating any executor, event, task or initialization.
The native export subprocess must actually start before the verifier initialization event is set.
OpenUSD and NumPy initialization remains inside the clock, including the first cold sample.
Only after durable native export returns may USD validation or the fresh native query begin.
The independent full USD comparison and full fresh-query equality may overlap. Neither may sample, omit data, change expected values or use product output as a reference.
Retrieve every future result. Record every initialization, query and validation error. No acknowledgment or submission is completion.
Join every executor worker before stopping the clock. Preserve all actual native PID/wait/exit receipts.
A native launch/export error fails. Failure before the spawn signal must release and join the initialization waiter; it must not hang or pass.
A query, initialization or validation error keeps the sample failed even if other concurrent work succeeds.
All six samples, original 100k/200k workloads, 250/500ms core limits, 2000/4000ms total limits and full1e-6/discrete comparisons remain.
Diagnostic operation times may overlap and are never subtracted from elapsed wall time. No preclock warmup, cached-result substitution or cold exception.
Both Mac architectures remain required. New concurrency controls are helper evidence only, not product acceptance.
independent_control_cases: initialization starts after native-start signal and overlaps export
query and validation both finish before return
query failure is retained while validation still completes
validation failure is retained while query still completes
native launch failure releases and joins waiter

sources.rule: The executor context waits for pending work; result retrieves task outcome and raises task exceptions.
Event communicates a condition; it never establishes successful task completion. Threads do not guarantee CPU parallelism under the GIL.
